milestones.title: Editorial Portfolio Redesign
milestones.vision: Replace the existing cosmic terminal portfolio with a premium one-page editorial portfolio: Spectral now as the Plantin-like serif, warm cream paper background, restrained ink palette, smooth Lenis and GSAP scroll choreography, real content from cv.md only, and a designed GitHub activity dashboard that treats the user's public work as the centerpiece.
success_criteria: Homepage no longer uses the matrix rain, cosmic gradient, terminal colors, JetBrains Mono identity, typewriter gimmick, card-grid portfolio pattern, or floating social buttons.
The page renders as one editorial scroll with Opening, Lede, Selected Work, Experience, GitHub Activity, Things I Find Cool, and Colophon sections.
Spectral is used as the primary Plantin-like serif; UI labels use a minimal supporting sans only where needed; colors are warm paper, warm ink, muted gray, and restrained oxblood accent.
Lenis and GSAP ScrollTrigger provide smooth scroll and section choreography while honoring prefers-reduced-motion.
Selected Work contains only Reliu and NazScan, using the user's exact positioning: Reliu zero to TestFlight ready, NazScan tried building a one command security scanner for vibe-coded repos.
Personal content is traceable to career-ops/cv.md or explicit user-provided wording; no unsupported companies, roles, projects, or claims are introduced.
GitHub activity is fetched at build time into a static artifact and rendered as a designed dashboard without exposing tokens to the client bundle.

The redesigned site builds successfully, runs locally, has no browser console errors, and passes focused accessibility checks for landmarks, keyboard navigation, focus states, contrast, and reduced motion.

key_risks.risk: Visual taste risk: minimal editorial can become plain if typography, spacing, and motion are not tuned together.
key_risks.whyItMatters: The user's core concern is avoiding AI slop; a technically correct rebuild that feels generic fails the goal.

key_risks.risk: Motion risk: Lenis and GSAP can make the page feel expensive or can harm accessibility and performance if overdone.
key_risks.whyItMatters: The user wants smooth novel-like scroll but the site must remain usable, responsive, and reduced-motion safe.

key_risks.risk: Data risk: GitHub tokens or API failures could leak secrets or break the static site.
key_risks.whyItMatters: The dashboard is central to the concept, but secret handling and graceful fallback are non-negotiable.

key_risks.risk: Content trust risk: unsupported resume claims could reappear if older portfolio files or unrelated career files are used.
key_risks.whyItMatters: The user explicitly corrected hallucinated work history and constrained the source of truth to cv.md.

proof_strategy.whatWillBeProven: the live homepage shell shows the paper, serif, opening spread, lede, and section rhythm without legacy visual noise
Lenis and GSAP scroll choreography works in browser and reduced-motion mode remains readable and non-jarring
selected work and timeline are rendered from curated content traceable to cv.md and user copy only
a build-time fetch writes static data with fallback behavior and no token in the client bundle
the final running site passes build, browser assertions, console checks, accessibility checks, and visual review

# S01: Editorial Shell and Visual Language

**Replaced the cosmic terminal app with a live cream editorial shell: Spectral serif, warm paper tokens, semantic section order, and a 10-test regression suite guarding against legacy re-introduction.**

## What Happened

S01 replaced the existing matrix/cosmic/terminal React app with a fully wired editorial shell across three tasks.

**T01 — Design tokens and font loading:** The Inter-only global CSS was replaced with a dual-font system (Spectral 300/400/500/600 regular + italic, Inter as supporting sans). CSS custom properties define the entire palette: --color-paper (#f5f1eb warm cream), --color-ink, --color-surface, --color-muted, --color-oxblood (#7a1d1d), --color-hairline. Tailwind was wired to reference these via var() rather than hardcoded values. Focus-visible uses oxblood outline for on-brand accessibility. Reduced-motion, skip-link, and font-smoothing defaults were all established. Build passed with no errors; CSS bundle grew from ~3.87 kB to ~4.69 kB gzip as expected.

**T02 — App shell rewire:** App.js was stripped of all old imports (MatrixRain, Header, HeroSection, AboutSection, EducationExperienceSection, ProjectsSection, Footer) and rewired to render EditorialPortfolio.jsx only. The new shell delivers semantic sections in the agreed order (opening/#about, lede, #projects/work, #experience, #education, #skills, github, cool, colophon) with alternating --color-paper / --color-surface backgrounds for visual rhythm. A skip-link targeting #main and a stable main landmark are present. JS bundle shrank by 8.69 kB gzip (46.47 kB from 55.16 kB), confirming full elimination of old components.

**T03 — Editorial spread components and shell test:** OpeningSpread.jsx and SectionShell.jsx were extracted as standalone components. SectionShell accepts a `surface` prop ('paper' | 'surface') for the alternating background pattern. EditorialPortfolio was refactored to compose from these. A 10-test Jest suite was added in src/__tests__/editorial-shell.test.js covering: identity heading ("Aatif"), all named section anchors (#about, #experience, #projects, #education, #skills, colophon footer, skip link targeting #main, lede headline), and a source-file read assertion that detects re-introduction of legacy terminal/matrix imports. All 10 tests pass.

## Verification

1. **npm run build** (node exec, exit 0): "Compiled successfully." JS bundle 46.51 kB gzip, CSS 4.73 kB. No errors, no type failures.
2. **npx react-scripts test --watchAll=false --testPathPattern=editorial-shell --forceExit** (exit 0): 10/10 tests pass in editorial-shell.test.js in 3.003 s. Only output besides PASS lines is a known CRA/React 18 ReactDOMTestUtils.act() deprecation warning — not a test failure.

## Requirements Advanced

- R001 — Cosmic/terminal visual system fully removed from the active app path; editorial token system, Spectral typography, and warm paper palette are now the live rendering surface consumed by all subsequent slices.

CRA's pinned @testing-library/react emits a ReactDOMTestUtils.act() deprecation warning on React 18. Not a test failure; requires upgrading @testing-library/react to 14+ which needs ejecting or overriding CRA dependency resolution. Safe to ignore through S06.

- `src/index.css` — Replaced Inter-only CSS with full editorial token system: CSS custom properties for palette, typography, spacing, focus-visible, skip-link, reduced-motion

# S01 UAT: Editorial Shell and Visual Language

**UAT Type:** Integration — verifies the live editorial shell renders correctly in a browser and the build pipeline is clean.

## Preconditions

- Node.js and npm are installed.
- Working directory is `C:/Users/smati/VS Code Projects/aatif_website`.
- Dependencies are installed (`npm install` has been run).

## Steps and Expected Outcomes

1. **Run the build**
   ```
   npm run build
   ```
   **Expected:** Terminal prints "Compiled successfully." with no errors. JS bundle is ~46–47 kB gzip; CSS bundle is ~4–5 kB gzip.

2. **Run the test suite**
   ```
   npx react-scripts test --watchAll=false --testPathPattern=editorial-shell --forceExit
   ```
   **Expected:** "Tests: 10 passed, 10 total" with exit code 0. The only console output besides PASS lines is a React 18 act() deprecation warning (known, non-blocking).

3. **Start the dev server**
   ```
   npm start
   ```
   **Expected:** Browser opens at localhost:3000. Page background is warm cream (not black/dark). No matrix rain, no terminal colors, no cosmic gradient, no typewriter animation.

4. **Inspect typography**
   Open DevTools → Elements. Verify `body` or `:root` uses `--font-serif: 'Spectral', serif` and the page headings render in Spectral (not JetBrains Mono or system sans-serif).

5. **Inspect color tokens**
   In DevTools → Computed styles on `<html>` or `:root`, verify CSS custom properties: `--color-paper`, `--color-ink`, `--color-oxblood`, `--color-muted`, `--color-hairline` are defined with warm values (paper ≈ #f5f1eb, oxblood ≈ #7a1d1d).

6. **Verify section order in DOM**
   In DevTools → Elements, confirm the following section IDs exist in order: `#about`, `#experience`, `#projects`, `#education`, `#skills`. A colophon footer element is also present.

7. **Verify skip link**
   Tab once from the top of the page. A "Skip to content" link should become visible (focus-visible style) and target `#main`.

8. **Verify no legacy components**
   In DevTools → Sources, confirm `MatrixRain`, `Header`, `HeroSection`, `AboutSection`, `EducationExperienceSection`, `ProjectsSection`, and `Footer` are not loaded in the JS bundle.

9. **Verify focus styles**
   Tab through interactive elements. Each focused element shows an oxblood (#7a1d1d) outline, not the browser default blue ring.

10. **Check browser console**
    DevTools → Console should show zero errors. No "Cannot find module", no React render errors, no network 404s for fonts.

## Edge Cases

- **Reduced motion:** With `prefers-reduced-motion: reduce` set in OS/browser, page should still render correctly (no invisible or missing content — motion suppression is a CSS-only default at this stage, active animation is S02 scope).
- **Narrow viewport (375px):** Page text should wrap gracefully with no horizontal scroll; sections stack vertically.

## What Happened

Both `lenis` (^1.3.23) and `gsap` (^3.15.0) were already present in package.json — no install step needed. Created `src/hooks/useEditorialMotion.js` as the single entry point for all scroll choreography. The hook: (1) reads `prefers-reduced-motion` at call time, (2) always stamps `data-reduced-motion="true|false"` on `<html>` so CSS and downstream components can branch without re-running the media query, (3) dynamically imports Lenis inside the effect (keeps the bundle split-friendly and lets init failures be caught), (4) wires Lenis into the GSAP ticker via `gsap.ticker.add` with `lagSmoothing(0)` so ScrollTrigger stays frame-accurate, (5) proxies scroll events from Lenis through `ScrollTrigger.scrollerProxy` so all future GSAP scroll animations work correctly, (6) cleans up on unmount by calling `lenis.destroy()`, removing the ticker function, and calling `ScrollTrigger.killAll()` + `clearScrollMemory()`, (7) catches any init failure and logs a concise non-secret `console.error` in non-production environments only. When reduced-motion is active the effect returns immediately after setting the data attribute — no Lenis or GSAP calls are made.

tasks.title: Added 11-test reduced-motion guard suite for useEditorialMotion; fixed Jest ESM blockers for gsap and lenis via moduleNameMapper and manual mock
tasks.one_liner: Added 11-test reduced-motion guard suite for useEditorialMotion; fixed Jest ESM blockers for gsap and lenis via moduleNameMapper and manual mock
tasks.narrative:
The task required verifying that useEditorialMotion correctly skips Lenis and GSAP when prefers-reduced-motion is active, and adding a focused test suite to lock in that behavior.

**Hook analysis:** The hook already had a correct reduced-motion guard at line 38 — it reads `window.matchMedia('(prefers-reduced-motion: reduce)').matches` synchronously, stamps `data-reduced-motion` on `<html>`, and returns early before the dynamic `import('lenis')` call. CSS in index.css uses `html[data-reduced-motion='true']` to override `will-change` and a `@media (prefers-reduced-motion: reduce)` block to collapse all transitions. No content is hidden in reduced-motion mode — GSAP inline `opacity:0` only applies in normal-motion mode, and only after JS has confirmed motion is live.

**Jest ESM blockers:** Two ESM-only packages caused test failures: lenis ships only a `.mjs` bundle (no CJS fallback in its `main` field), and gsap/ScrollTrigger uses ESM imports. CRA's jest config has `transformIgnorePatterns` that blocks transforming node_modules, and `moduleFileExtensions` that excludes `.mjs`. Fix: added `moduleNameMapper` in package.json to redirect `lenis` → `__mocks__/lenis.js` (a CommonJS manual mock) and `gsap/ScrollTrigger` / `gsap` → their CJS dist builds. Also added `src/setupTests.js` with a global `matchMedia` stub so `gsap.registerPlugin(ScrollTrigger)` doesn't throw when the real CJS gsap loads at module scope.

**resetMocks conflict:** CRA's jest config sets `resetMocks: true`, which wipes mock implementations between tests — this broke the Lenis constructor mock since `jest.fn(() => instance)` had its implementation cleared. Fixed by setting `resetMocks: false` in the package.json jest override.

**Test suites written (11 tests total):**
- Reduced-motion guard (7): `data-reduced-motion="true"` stamped, `data-motion-ready` absent, Lenis not constructed, `gsap.fromTo` not called, `reducedMotion: true` returned, no inline opacity on reveal/hero elements
- Normal-motion path (3): `data-reduced-motion="false"` stamped, `reducedMotion: false` returned, Lenis constructed
- CSS contract (1): elements have no inline opacity before hook runs

**Side fix:** The `editorial-shell.test.js` was already failing (pre-existing, caused by T02 wiring gsap/ScrollTrigger into EditorialPortfolio). The moduleNameMapper + setupTests.js additions also fixed that suite as a side effect, restoring it to passing.

# T03: Added 11-test reduced-motion guard suite for useEditorialMotion; fixed Jest ESM blockers for gsap and lenis via moduleNameMapper and manual mock

**Added 11-test reduced-motion guard suite for useEditorialMotion; fixed Jest ESM blockers for gsap and lenis via moduleNameMapper and manual mock**

## What Happened

The task required verifying that useEditorialMotion correctly skips Lenis and GSAP when prefers-reduced-motion is active, and adding a focused test suite to lock in that behavior.

**Hook analysis:** The hook already had a correct reduced-motion guard at line 38 — it reads `window.matchMedia('(prefers-reduced-motion: reduce)').matches` synchronously, stamps `data-reduced-motion` on `<html>`, and returns early before the dynamic `import('lenis')` call. CSS in index.css uses `html[data-reduced-motion='true']` to override `will-change` and a `@media (prefers-reduced-motion: reduce)` block to collapse all transitions. No content is hidden in reduced-motion mode — GSAP inline `opacity:0` only applies in normal-motion mode, and only after JS has confirmed motion is live.

**Jest ESM blockers:** Two ESM-only packages caused test failures: lenis ships only a `.mjs` bundle (no CJS fallback in its `main` field), and gsap/ScrollTrigger uses ESM imports. CRA's jest config has `transformIgnorePatterns` that blocks transforming node_modules, and `moduleFileExtensions` that excludes `.mjs`. Fix: added `moduleNameMapper` in package.json to redirect `lenis` → `__mocks__/lenis.js` (a CommonJS manual mock) and `gsap/ScrollTrigger` / `gsap` → their CJS dist builds. Also added `src/setupTests.js` with a global `matchMedia` stub so `gsap.registerPlugin(ScrollTrigger)` doesn't throw when the real CJS gsap loads at module scope.

**resetMocks conflict:** CRA's jest config sets `resetMocks: true`, which wipes mock implementations between tests — this broke the Lenis constructor mock since `jest.fn(() => instance)` had its implementation cleared. Fixed by setting `resetMocks: false` in the package.json jest override.

**Test suites written (11 tests total):**
- Reduced-motion guard (7): `data-reduced-motion="true"` stamped, `data-motion-ready` absent, Lenis not constructed, `gsap.fromTo` not called, `reducedMotion: true` returned, no inline opacity on reveal/hero elements
- Normal-motion path (3): `data-reduced-motion="false"` stamped, `reducedMotion: false` returned, Lenis constructed
- CSS contract (1): elements have no inline opacity before hook runs

**Side fix:** The `editorial-shell.test.js` was already failing (pre-existing, caused by T02 wiring gsap/ScrollTrigger into EditorialPortfolio). The moduleNameMapper + setupTests.js additions also fixed that suite as a side effect, restoring it to passing.

## Verification

Ran `npm test -- --watchAll=false --testPathPattern=editorial-motion --forceExit`. All 11 tests pass in ~3s. Also ran the full test suite: editorial-motion (11/11 pass), editorial-shell (9/9 pass, restored from pre-existing failure). GitHubService has 1 pre-existing failure unrelated to this task (confirmed via git stash before/after).

## Deviations

Added src/setupTests.js (not in the task plan's expected output list) to provide a global matchMedia stub — required because gsap's CJS dist calls matchMedia at module load time via registerPlugin(ScrollTrigger). Also added __mocks__/lenis.js to resolve the lenis ESM-only bundle issue. package.json jest config was extended with moduleNameMapper and resetMocks:false. These additions were necessary to make any tests runnable in the Jest/JSDOM environment and are not feature changes.
